#: citare's supplement to reporters-db's laws.json, merged in by crates/citare-core/build.rs.

Each entry is one more cluster under its key, in laws.json's schema. Under a key reporters-db has, a missing name, cite_type, jurisdiction, start, end or regexes comes from that key's first cluster, so the entry adds spellings of the same edition. A new key gives them all.
strings: prefilter strings (compared with whitespace removed) for a regex that doesn't contain the reporter's name; without them it would run on every document.
examples: citations the entry must recognize; crates/citare-core/tests/law_local.rs checks each one.
Why each entry exists, and how the forms were measured: docs/laws-local.md.

Ala. Code.notes: Alabama's own style, with the code's year.

regexes: (?P<reporter>(?P<subject>Pen\.|Civ\.|Evid\.|Veh\.|Gov\.|Fam\.|Lab\.|Ins\.|Prob\.|Corp\.|Com\.|Elec\.|Ed\.|Educ\.|Fin\.|Wat\.|Bus\. & Prof\.|Welf\. & Inst\.|Health & Saf\.|Rev\. & Tax\.|Pub\. Resources|Pub\. Util\.|Fish & G\.|Food & Agr\.|Harb\. & Nav\.|Sts\. & Hy\.|Unemp\. Ins\.) Code), § $law_section
Cal. Code.notes: California Style Manual: the code by subject without `Cal.`, and a comma before the section. The comma and the abbreviated subject keep it apart from Texas's `Penal Code § 22.01`.
California Style Manual's `Code Civ. Proc.`; the code is Cal. Civ. Proc. Code.

Conn. Gen. Stat..notes: Connecticut courts cite their statutes as `General Statutes §`, often with the revision year.

Conn. Practice Book.name: Connecticut Practice Book
Conn. Practice Book.notes: The rules of Connecticut's courts. reporters-db has no court rules.

Ga. Code Ann..notes: Georgia courts' Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

La. Stat. Ann..notes: Louisiana Revised Statutes, the form before the Bluebook's `La. Stat. Ann.`.

Mass. Gen. Laws.notes: Massachusetts courts' `G. L. c. N, §`, and chapters with a letter (93A), which reporters-db's `ch\. (?P<chapter>\d+)` misses.

Me. Rev. Stat. Ann..notes: Maine courts put the title first, and titles can have a letter (19-A).

regexes: (?P<reporter>(?P<subject>Family Ct\.? Act|Family Court Act|Surrogate's Court Procedure Act|SCPA|CPLR|C\.P\.L\.R\.)),? § $law_section
N.Y..notes: New York's codes not named `Law`, cited without `N.Y.`.

regexes: (?P<reporter>(?P<subject>Abandoned Property|Agriculture and Markets|Alcoholic Beverage Control|Arts and Cultural Affairs|Banking|Benevolent Orders|Business Corporation|Canal|Cannabis|Civil Rights|Civil Service|Cooperative Corporations|Correction|County|Criminal Procedure|Debtor and Creditor|Domestic Relations|Economic Development|Education|Elder|Election|Eminent Domain Procedure|Employers' Liability|Energy|Environmental Conservation|Estates, Powers and Trusts|Executive|Financial Services|General Associations|General Business|General City|General Construction|General Municipal|General Obligations|Highway|Indian|Insurance|Judiciary|Labor|Legislative|Lien|Limited Liability Company|Local Finance|Mental Hygiene|Military|Multiple Dwelling|Multiple Residence|Municipal Home Rule|Navigation|Not-for-Profit Corporation|Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation|Partnership|Penal|Personal Property|Private Housing Finance|Public Authorities|Public Buildings|Public Health|Public Housing|Public Lands|Public Officers|Public Service|Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding|Railroad|Rapid Transit|Real Property Actions and Proceedings|Real Property Tax|Real Property|Religious Corporations|Retirement and Social Security|Rural Electric Cooperative|Second Class Cities|Social Services|State Finance|Tax|Town|Transportation Corporations|Transportation|Vehicle and Traffic|Village|Volunteer Firefighters' Benefit|Workers' Compensation) Law),? § $law_section
examples: Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law § 1304
N.Y. Law.notes: New York's consolidated laws cited by name without `N.Y.`, as New York courts write them. The list is the consolidated laws' names, so `Family Law` or `Criminal Law` (Maryland articles) don't match.

Okla. Stat..notes: Oklahoma courts put the title first and the code's year after `O.S.`.

Pa. Cons. Stat..notes: Pennsylvania courts' abbreviation of the Consolidated Statutes.

Pa. Stat. Ann..name: Purdon's Pennsylvania Statutes Annotated
Pa. Stat. Ann..notes: Pennsylvania statutes not yet in the Consolidated Statutes, cited by Purdon's title. reporters-db has no entry.

examples: TEX. CIV. PRAC. & REM. CODE ANN. § 16.026(a)
Tex. Code Ann..notes: Texas codes typeset in small capitals (all capitals in text), without `Ann.`, or without a space before `Code`.

Vt. Stat. Ann..notes: Vermont courts put the title first.

W. Va. Code.notes: The code's name spelled out, as West Virginia courts often write it.

Wis. Stat..notes: Small capitals, as Wisconsin courts typeset it.
